description: Group only the examinations that have a patient ID; the total and the average share use only those; list up to 10 above-average groups by excess share.

a.request: Group the examination records by patient `ID`, leaving out examinations that have no patient ID. For each group, count its examinations and work out that count as a fraction of the total over all groups. For the groups whose fraction is above the average fraction across groups, list the ID, the number of examinations, the fraction, and how much the fraction exceeds the average, sorted by that excess from largest to smallest, top 10 only, unrounded.
a.sql: WITH examination_counts AS (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS examination_count FROM Examination WHERE ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ID), fractions AS (SELECT ID, examination_count, examination_count * 1.0 / SUM(examination_count) OVER () AS fraction FROM examination_counts), deviations AS (SELECT ID, examination_count, fraction, fraction - AVG(fraction) OVER () AS excess FROM fractions) SELECT ID, examination_count, fraction, excess FROM deviations WHERE excess > 0 ORDER BY excess DESC LIMIT 10;

b.request: Group Examination records with a non-null patient ID by ID; for each ID, calculate its examination count and its unrounded share of all examinations with a non-null patient ID. Return up to 10 IDs whose share exceeds the average share across those ID groups, showing the ID, count, share, and excess over the average share, ordered by excess descending
b.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS examination_count FROM Examination WHERE ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ID), shares AS (SELECT ID, examination_count, examination_count * 1.0 / SUM(examination_count) OVER () AS share FROM counts), average_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS value FROM shares) SELECT s.ID, s.examination_count, s.share, s.share - a.value AS excess_over_average FROM shares AS s CROSS JOIN average_share AS a WHERE s.share > a.value ORDER BY excess_over_average DESC LIMIT 10

c.request: Break the examination records down by patient ID. Which IDs have an above-average share of the examinations? Show the ID, its number of examinations, its share of the total, and how far above the average share it is, listing the top 10 by that margin from largest to smallest, unrounded. Group only the examinations that have a patient ID; the total and the average share use only those; list up to 10 above-average groups by excess share.
c.sql: WITH exam_counts AS (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS examination_count FROM Examination WHERE ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ID), totals AS (SELECT SUM(examination_count) AS total_examinations, COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM exam_counts) SELECT e.ID, e.examination_count, 1.0 * e.examination_count / t.total_examinations AS share, 1.0 * e.examination_count / t.total_examinations - 1.0 / t.patient_count AS excess_share FROM exam_counts AS e CROSS JOIN totals AS t WHERE 1.0 * e.examination_count / t.total_examinations > 1.0 / t.patient_count ORDER BY excess_share DESC, e.ID ASC LIMIT 10;

d.request: Among examination records with a patient ID, which patient IDs have an above-average share of examinations? Calculate the total and average share using only those records, and list up to 10 IDs by excess share, largest first. Show each ID, its examination count, its share of the total, and how far that share exceeds the average, without rounding.
d.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS examination_count FROM Examination WHERE ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ID), totals AS (SELECT SUM(examination_count) AS total_examinations, COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM counts) SELECT c.ID, c.examination_count, 1.0 * c.examination_count / t.total_examinations AS share_of_total, 1.0 * c.examination_count / t.total_examinations - 1.0 / t.patient_count AS excess_share FROM counts AS c CROSS JOIN totals AS t WHERE 1.0 * c.examination_count / t.total_examinations > 1.0 / t.patient_count ORDER BY excess_share DESC, c.ID LIMIT 10;
